  BIG HILL SUBSTATION 765-

          PROJECT
                                         PUC DOCKET NO. 59475
                 BRIEF ON REMAND PRELIMINARY ORDER ISSUES 11 AND 13

TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:
        Christine Thies, appearing pro se, submits this Brief regarding Preliminary Order Issues 11 and
13. The Commission’s questions are specific: whether the proposed facilities are necessary to meet state
or federal reliability standards, and what congestion-cost savings consumers may receive from those
facilities. The evidentiary record remains closed. The answers therefore must come from evidence already
in the record, not from assumptions about what inclusion in ERCOT’s broader transmission plan means.
SOAH Order No. 35 specifically kept the evidentiary record closed.


I. ISSUE 11 — THE RECORD DOES NOT ESTABLISH THAT THESE PARTICULAR
FACILITIES ARE NECESSARY TO MEET A RELIABILITY STANDARD
        ERCOT identified a need for additional transmission capacity. But that is not the question
presented by Issue 11. The question is whether Bell County East–Big Hill at 765 kV is necessary to
meet a state or federal reliability standard.

        ERCOT’s own Permian Basin Reliability Plan evaluated 345-kV, 500-kV, and 765-kV
alternatives and reported that all three satisfied the applicable ERCOT and NERC reliability criteria. The
alternatives provided different levels of transfer capability, but the record does not show that the 345-kV
or 500-kV alternatives failed the applicable reliability standards.

        Showing that 765 kV provides greater transfer capability or that ERCOT ultimately selected a
765-kV plan does not establish that this particular 765-kV facility is required to comply with a reliability
standard. Applicants’ own Directory also cites Mr. Gurley’s testimony acknowledging that he was not
                                                      1
 aware of a study isolating each import-path line independently because the lines were studied together. A
system-wide or portfolio study may demonstrate that several facilities collectively improve reliability, but
it does not necessarily establish that this individual CCN project is itself necessary to satisfy an identified
reliability standard.

        While ERCOT’s recommendation is important, it does not eliminate Applicants’ burden to
establish necessity for the facilities for which they seek a CCN. The record may establish a broader need
for additional transmission. It does not establish that Bell County East–Big Hill at 765 kV is necessary to
meet a state or federal reliability standard.


II. ISSUE 13 — THE RECORD DOES NOT QUANTIFY CONGESTION-COST SAVINGS
ATTRIBUTABLE TO THIS PROJECT
        Issue 13 asks for the estimated congestion-cost savings consumers may receive from the proposed
facilities. The record contains economic comparisons involving broader transmission plans, but it does
not provide a quantified estimate of congestion-cost savings attributable specifically to Bell County East–
Big Hill. The PFD itself recognized that Applicants did not provide a quantified estimate of congestion-
cost savings to consumers, and the statewide figures do not allocate those savings to Import Path 2.
Economic benefits associated with an entire transmission portfolio cannot automatically be treated as the
economic benefit of one individual project within that portfolio.

        Applicants therefore have not provided the project-specific calculation necessary to answer Issue
13 with a dollar amount attributable to these facilities.


III. CONCLUSION
        The remand does not require SOAH to reconsider the entire question of need. It asks SOAH to
expressly answer Issues 11 and 13 from the existing record.

        That record shows that multiple voltage alternatives satisfied the studied reliability criteria, but it
does not establish that this particular 765-kV facility is necessary to meet a state or federal reliability
standard. Likewise, the record contains broader economic projections but does not quantify congestion-
cost savings attributable specifically to Bell County East–Big Hill.

        Intervenor respectfully requests that the amended Proposal for Decision answer Issues 11 and 13
accordingly and maintain the recommendation that the CCN application be denied.
